content.content:
nohup node ./node_modules/next/dist/bin/next start -H 127.0.0.1 -p 3103 > ../ci-artifacts/empower-server.log 2>&1 &
          for attempt in $(seq 1 60); do curl -sf -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:3103/login && exit 0; sleep 1; done
          echo "Admin server did not become ready"; tail -50 ../ci-artifacts/empower-server.log; exit 1

      - name: Install Playwright Chromium
        run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium

      - name: Run Empower and partner onboarding browser journeys (B1.1 to B1.6, Launch Ready)
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE="$(node -e "console.log(require('playwright-core').chromium.executablePath())")" \
            npx playwright test -c playwright.empower.config.ts 2>&1 | tee ../ci-artifacts/empower-browser.log
          # The specs skip themselves without their variables; CI must never pass on a skipped journey.
          sed -E 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' ../ci-artifacts/empower-browser.log > ../ci-artifacts/empower-browser.plain.log
          grep -E "[0-9]+ passed" ../ci-artifacts/empower-browser.plain.log
          if grep -Eq "[0-9]+ (skipped|did not run)" ../ci-artifacts/empower-browser.plain.log; then echo "Empower browser journeys were skipped"; exit 1; fi

      - name: Upload Empower browser evidence and failure artifacts
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@330a01c490aca151604b8cf639adc76d48f6c5d4 # v5.0.0
        with:
          name: empower-browser-acceptance
          path: |
            ci-artifacts
            admin/test-results/empower
            docs/expansion/empower/evidence
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          retention-days: 14

  database:
    name: Database and Migrations
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 25
    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:16-alpine
        env:
          POSTGRES_DB: scalesmiths_integration_test
          POSTGRES_USER: scalesmiths_ci
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: REDACTED
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "pg_isready -U scalesmiths_ci -d scalesmiths_integration_test"
          --health-interval 5s --health-timeout 5s --health-retries 10
      # A second, dedicated database for the Expansion concurrency suite. Port 55440 and the name ss_expansion_test are exactly what that
      # suite's own safety guard accepts, so no guard is relaxed. It runs as the restricted runtime roles, never as the superuser.
      postgres-expansion:
        image: postgres:16-alpine
        env:
          POSTGRES_DB: ss_expansion_test
          POSTGRES_USER: scalesmiths_ci
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: REDACTED
        ports:
          - 55440:5432

s=s.replace(a,'.pl-summary{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fit,minmax(130px,1fr));gap:12px;margin:16px 0 20px}')

open(p,'w',encoding='utf8').write(s)
EOF

  - `src/lib/server/partner-pipeline.database.test.ts` (PGlite, 10 cases: off by default, isolation, non-enumeration, suspended partner, timeline privacy, append-only, validation, DB owner guard, follow-up, meetings): pass when run on its own.

- **Deployment status:** not deployed; switch off.

## B2.2 – B2.7: Not started

content.text:
B2.1 now has its browser evidence. A new Journey A and E browser test passes in CI against a production build and a disposable database. CI on the latest head (screenshots and docs only) is still running; the previous head was green apart from one Web job that was still running.

**What the test covers** (`admin/test/e2e/ascend-pipeline.spec.ts`, run by the existing Empower Browser Acceptance job):
- **Journey A:**
  - The registered prospect lands in the "New" column. Board, table and list views all work, and so do search, stage, "needs my action" and sort.
  - Keyboard: opening the detail dialog moves focus into it, Tab stays inside, Escape closes it, and focus returns to the card.
  - The partner can make only the allowed stage moves, and each other stage shows its reason.
  - Recording an interaction and setting a follow-up date work.
  - A founder-help request reaches the founder queue. The founder's confirmation shows up for the partner, without the founder's private note.
  - The commission ledger is unchanged.
- **Journey E:** another partner gets "not found" when reading, adding a note, setting a follow-up or forcing a stage change on Partner A's prospect. A partner cannot set "approved" on their own prospect. Founder-only pages, revoked sessions and anonymous requests are all refused, and the ledger is unchanged.
- **Accessibility:** axe (WCAG 2.2 AA, serious and critical) found no violations on the board, table or dialog. No page scrolls sideways at any width.

**Four problems the screenshots showed, now fixed:**
- The guidance panel inside the dialog kept showing "Registered" after the prospect moved to discovery; it now refreshes after a stage move.
- Meeting rows showed raw text such as "technical scoping / requested"; they now read "Technical scoping / Meeting requested".
- The summary cards touched the header block, and on phones they took one row each.
- The shared partner header cut off "SCALESMITHS" between 641 and 1100 px. That was already happening on the existing B1.6 pages, and the fix applies to them too.

I also made two smaller wording fixes: a backwards stage now gives a specific reason, and the "update discovery" link no longer breaks its sentence.

The 30 screenshots (board, table, list, dialog top and dialog history at 320, 390, 768, 1024, 1440 and 1920 px) are committed in `docs/expansion/ascend/evidence/b2-1/`. I looked at all of them after the last run. `B2-IMPLEMENTATION-STATUS.md`, the security model and the [#166](https://github.com/TheFridey/ScaleSmiths/pull/166) description now record this.

**Still not done:** no manual screen-reader pass, and reduced motion is only checked by reading the CSS. The Admin Forge E2E check failed once on #166 in the known intermittent test that #164 fixes, and passed on later heads.

s=s.replace(a,'''## B2.2 Intelligent prospect qualification: Implemented (browser evidence pending CI)

- **Branch:** `feature/operation-ascend-b2-2`, stacked on B2.1 (`feature/operation-ascend-b2`). The draft PR targets `master` so the full CI runs; review it after #166.
- **Implementation:**
  - `admin/src/lib/partner-qualification.ts`: six equally weighted, declared readiness factors over existing discovery fields, with suggested questions (`discoveryGaps`) and escalation (`guidancePlanFor` plus `technicalReviewFlags`).
  - `admin/src/lib/server/expansion-qualification.ts` and `GET /api/expansion/qualification` (founder inspection).
  - A partner checklist in the pipeline dialog and a founder panel on each opportunity (`QualificationChecklist`, `FounderQualification`).
  - Policy rule `ascend.qualification`.

## Summary

Operation Ascend B2.2, switched off by `PARTNER_QUALIFICATION_ENABLED`. **Stacked on #166 (B2.1): review and merge #166 first; this PR's own changes are the last commit.** Partners see, inside the pipeline dialog, six equally weighted readiness factors derived from their recorded discovery answers. Each factor says why it matters and what would meet it, followed by questions to ask next and suggested founder involvement that pre-selects the help request. Founders inspect the same factors on each opportunity. Duplicate detection also now treats spelling variants of a company ("Smith & Sons Ltd" / "The Smith and Sons Limited") and an already-held company number as existing relationships.

## Type

- [x] `feat`
- [ ] `fix`
- [x] `test`
- [x] `docs`
- [ ] `refactor`
- [ ] `security`
- [ ] `perf`
- [ ] `chore`

## Scope

- [ ] Public web
- [x] Admin
- [ ] Forge
- [x] Database/migrations
- [ ] Docker/deployment/Nginx
- [x] CI/tooling
- [ ] Documentation only

## Validation

Commands run, with results:

```text
npx vitest run src/lib/partner-qualification.test.ts src/lib/business-name-key.database.test.ts src/lib/server/expansion.test.ts  -> 48 passed (incl. all 38 existing Expansion cases)
npx vitest run expansion-qualification.database + partner-pipeline.database + partner-qualification + rbac-authorization       -> 73 passed
npx eslint <changed files>                                                                                                       -> clean
npx tsc --noEmit                                                                                                                 -> no project errors
npm run test:db:migrate on disposable PostgreSQL 16.14 and 14.25                                                                 -> "admin 100/100" on both; PG14 expansion_business_name_key('The Smith & Sons Ltd.') = smithandsons
node scripts/check-migration-history.mjs                                                                                         -> "52 historical and 73 forward migrations are locked"
```

Commands not run, and why:

```text
Browser journey (qualification step added to ascend-pipeline.spec.ts): runs in CI's Empower Browser Acceptance on this PR; results to be added as a comment.
Full admin unit suite locally: machine too slow; CI's Admin job is authoritative.
```

## Migrations

- [ ] No database migration.
- [x] Migration included and documented below.

`0099_ascend_business_name_key` (after B2.1's 0098): forward-only and additive. It adds an `IMMUTABLE PARALLEL SAFE` SQL function `expansion_business_name_key(text)` and expression indexes `prospects_business_name_key_idx` and `clients_business_name_key_idx`. Registration matches on the new key **or** the previous plain key, so no earlier match is lost. It is registered in the journal, the shared plan and the checksum manifest. Index build time on production `prospects`/`clients` is not measured. Both tables are small CRM tables today, but this needs a look before Gate A.

## Environment

- [ ] No environment-variable change.
- [x] Environment variables added to `.env.example` and documented below.

`PARTNER_QUALIFICATION_ENABLED` (admin app, default `false`): partner detail returns `qualification: null` and the founder API returns 404 while it is off.

## Security and Privacy

- [x] No secrets, provider credentials, real `.env` files, database dumps, or
      client-private exports are included.
- [x] Admin/Forge access control and generated-workspace isolation are preserved.
- [x] Public analytics remains minimised and consent-aware.

The new founder endpoint has policy rule `ascend.qualification` (`expansion.manage`), re-checked against the live session; partners are refused. Factors read only declared discovery fields; personal or unknown keys change nothing (tested). The checklist is display only: nothing writes it, and no ownership, scope, approval or commission rule reads it. Duplicate matches return the existing generic 409 and never reveal which record matched.

## Evidence

The browser journey now also covers qualification:
- the partner sees "3 of 6", the honest notice and per-factor states;
- "Ask for technical scoping" pre-selects and focuses the help form;
- axe passes on the dialog;
- the founder API returns the same factors and refuses partners;
- the founder sees "Qualification readiness (how it is derived)" on the opportunity;
- the opportunity status is unchanged.

Screenshots: `qualification-partner-<width>.png` and `qualification-founder-1440.png` in the CI artifact.

## Residual Risk and Follow-up

- FD-ASC-06: scope submission still requires a budget answer (existing rule); the directive treats budget as voluntary. Unchanged pending a founder decision.
- Subdomain/registrable-domain duplicates are not detected (needs a public-suffix list). There is no founder queue for near-miss names: matches get the existing "contact commercial support" response.
- B2.3 to B2.7 not started.

## Rollback

Revert the commit. The switch is off. Migration 0099 is additive: reverted code no longer calls the function, and the function and indexes are harmless if left. There is no down-migration (forward-only policy).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF

## Summary

Operation Ascend B2.2, switched off by `PARTNER_QUALIFICATION_ENABLED`. **Stacked on #166 (B2.1): review and merge #166 first; this PR's own changes are the last commit.** Partners see, inside the pipeline dialog, six equally weighted readiness factors derived from their recorded discovery answers. Founders inspect the same factors on each opportunity. Duplicate detection also now treats spelling variants of a company ("Smith & Sons Ltd" / "The Smith and Sons Limited") and an already-held company number as existing relationships.

## Type

- [x] `feat`
- [ ] `fix`
- [x] `test`
- [x] `docs`
- [ ] `refactor`
- [ ] `security`
- [ ] `perf`
- [ ] `chore`

- [ ] Public web
- [x] Admin
- [ ] Forge

- [ ] Docker/deployment/Nginx
- [x] CI/tooling
- [ ] Documentation only

## Validation

Commands run, with results:

```text
npx vitest run src/lib/partner-qualification.test.ts src/lib/business-name-key.database.test.ts src/lib/server/expansion.test.ts  -> 48 passed (incl. all 38 existing Expansion cases)
npx vitest run expansion-qualification.database + partner-pipeline.database + partner-qualification + rbac-authorization       -> 73 passed
npx eslint <changed files>                                                                                                       -> clean
npx tsc --noEmit                                                                                                                 -> no project errors
npm run test:db:migrate on disposable PostgreSQL 16.14 and 14.25                                                                 -> "admin 100/100" on both; PG14 expansion_business_name_key('The Smith & Sons Ltd.') = smithandsons
node scripts/check-migration-history.mjs                                                                                         -> "52 historical and 73 forward migrations are locked"
```

Commands not run, and why:

```text
Browser journey (qualification step added to ascend-pipeline.spec.ts): runs in CI's Empower Browser Acceptance on this PR; results to be added as a comment.
Full admin unit suite locally: machine too slow; CI's Admin job is authoritative.
```

## Migrations

- [ ] No database migration.
- [x] Migration included and documented below.

`0099_ascend_business_name_key` (after B2.1's 0098): forward-only and additive. It adds an `IMMUTABLE PARALLEL SAFE` SQL function `expansion_business_name_key(text)` and expression indexes `prospects_business_name_key_idx` and `clients_business_name_key_idx`. Registration matches on the new key **or** the previous plain key, so no earlier match is lost. It is registered in the journal, the shared plan and the checksum manifest. Index build time on production `prospects`/`clients` is not measured. Both tables are small CRM tables today, but this needs a look before Gate A.

## Environment

- [ ] No environment-variable change.
- [x] Environment variables added to `.env.example` and documented below.

`PARTNER_QUALIFICATION_ENABLED` (admin app, default `false`): partner detail returns `qualification: null` and the founder API returns 404 while it is off.

## Security and Privacy

- [x] No secrets, provider credentials, real `.env` files, database dumps, or
      client-private exports are included.
- [x] Admin/Forge access control and generated-workspace isolation are preserved.
- [x] Public analytics remains minimised and consent-aware.

The new founder endpoint has policy rule `ascend.qualification` (`expansion.manage`), re-checked against the live session; partners are refused. Factors read only declared discovery fields; personal or unknown keys change nothing (tested). The checklist is display only: nothing writes it, and no ownership, scope, approval or commission rule reads it. Duplicate matches return the existing generic 409 and never reveal which record matched.

## Evidence

The browser journey now also covers qualification:
- the partner sees "3 of 6", the honest notice and per-factor states;
- "Ask for technical scoping" pre-selects and focuses the help form;
- axe passes on the dialog;
- the founder API returns the same factors and refuses partners;
- the founder sees "Qualification readiness (how it is derived)" on the opportunity;
- the opportunity status is unchanged.

Screenshots: `qualification-partner-<width>.png` and `qualification-founder-1440.png` in the CI artifact.

## Residual Risk and Follow-up

- FD-ASC-06: scope submission still requires a budget answer (existing rule); the directive treats budget as voluntary. Unchanged pending a founder decision.
- Subdomain/registrable-domain duplicates are not detected (needs a public-suffix list). There is no founder queue for near-miss names: matches get the existing "contact commercial support" response.
- B2.3 to B2.7 not started.

## Rollback

Revert the commit. The switch is off. Migration 0099 is additive: reverted code no longer calls the function, and the function and indexes are harmless if left. There is no down-migration (forward-only policy).

fix(ascend): grant the business-name key to the restricted admin role

Runtime roles get EXECUTE only on functions in ADMIN_FUNCTION_GRANTS, so
partner registration failed with 503 under the restricted role in the
browser acceptance job (local checks ran as the superuser). Reproduced
with CI's provisioning on a disposable PostgreSQL 16: after the grant,
verify-postgres-privileges passes and the admin role can call
expansion_business_name_key.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git push -q origin feature/operation-ascend-b2-2 2>&1 | tail -1; git log --oneline -1

content.text:
B2.2 is built and open as draft PR [#167](https://github.com/TheFridey/ScaleSmiths/pull/167), switched off by `PARTNER_QUALIFICATION_ENABLED`. Its browser journey passes in CI. CI on the final head, which only adds screenshots and docs, is still running. It's stacked on [#166](https://github.com/TheFridey/ScaleSmiths/pull/166), so it shows B2.1's changes too and should be reviewed after #166 merges.

**Qualification readiness**
- **Partners:** the pipeline dialog now shows six checks on the discovery answers they've recorded, for example "Business requirement identified" or "Timescale understood". Each one says whether it's met, why it matters and what would meet it.
- **Help suggestions:** below the checks are questions to ask next and suggested founder involvement. Its "Ask for technical scoping" button pre-selects that option in the help form.
- **Founders:** they see the same checks on each opportunity in `/expansion`, under "Qualification readiness (how it is derived)".
- **No hidden score:** it shows "3 of 6 recorded" and says plainly that it is not a prediction and never rejects a prospect. Nothing saves it and no rule reads it. Fields about a person are ignored, which is tested.

**Duplicate detection (migration 0099)**
- Spelling variants now count as the same business: "Smith & Sons Ltd" matches "The Smith and Sons Limited". Each existing prospect or client name is compared with both the old key and the new one, so nothing that matched before stops matching.
- A company number that's already held now gets the same "contact commercial support" response instead of a database error.
- The TypeScript and SQL versions of the name key give identical results on 31 test names. All 38 existing Expansion tests still pass.
- The migration applies cleanly on PostgreSQL 14 and 16.

**Fixed after CI caught it**
- **Registration returned 503:** the database role the app runs as couldn't call the new SQL function, because the repo grants function access from an explicit list. My local checks had run as the database superuser, so they missed it. I added the grant and reproduced CI's role setup locally to confirm it now passes.
- **Test fixes:** a leftover filter in my browser test hid the prospect, and the "Ask for…" buttons were splitting their sentence. Both are fixed, and the screenshots at all six widths look right now.

**Still open**
- **FD-ASC-06:** scope submission still requires a budget answer, which is an existing rule, while your brief treats budget as voluntary. I left the rule alone for you to decide.
- **Duplicates on subdomains:** these aren't caught yet.
- **Index build time:** the new indexes on the production prospects and clients tables haven't been timed; check before deployment.
- **B2.3 to B2.7:** not started.

-- Operation Launch Ready: an auditable record of every partner lifecycle email attempt.
-- One row per message, keyed by an idempotency key so a retried request never sends twice. The recipient is stored only as a
-- SHA-256 of the normalised address (no plaintext email here). Failed messages can be retried by a founder; invitation emails
-- cannot (the secret link is never stored), so a founder issues a new invitation instead.
CREATE TABLE partner_notifications (
 id uuid PRIMARY KEY,
 idempotency_key text NOT NULL UNIQUE CHECK (char_length(idempotency_key) BETWEEN 8 AND 200),
 kind text NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('application_received','information_requested','application_declined','invitation','activated','agreement_reissued')),
 application_id integer REFERENCES partner_applications(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
 partner_id uuid REFERENCES expansion_partners(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
 recipient_sha256 text NOT NULL CHECK (recipient_sha256 ~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$'),
 status text NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('sent','failed','not_configured','disabled')),
 failure_reason text CHECK (failure_reason IS NULL OR char_length(failure_reason) <= 200),
 attempts integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 CHECK (attempts BETWEEN 1 AND 10),
 actor_id uuid REFERENCES admin_users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
 created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
 updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE INDEX partner_notifications_application_idx ON partner_notifications (application_id, created_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX partner_notifications_partner_idx ON partner_notifications (partner_id, created_at DESC);

      expect((await api(p1.context, '/api/partner', { action: 'discovery', id: oppId, discovery: { objectives: 'Win more local enquiries online', pages: 'Home, services, contact', functionality: 'Online booking and payments', budget: 'Discussed with the owner', timescale: 'Spring', decisionProcess: 'Owner decides' } })).status).toBe(200)

      await form.getByLabel('Reason').fill('TEST ONLY takes technical scoping this week')

      // [API] A stale second assignment from an old view is refused; the partner keeps ownership.
      const stale = await api(founder.context, '/api/expansion/command', { action: 'assign', opportunityId: oppId, assigneeId: null, reason: 'TEST ONLY stale view', expectedCurrentId: null })
      expect(stale.status).toBe(409)
      expect((await su.query('select p.user_id from expansion_opportunities o join expansion_partners p on p.id=o.partner_id where o.id=$1', [oppId])).rows[0].user_id).toBe((await su.query('select id from admin_users where email=$1', [P1])).rows[0].id)
      // [UI] The queue item opens the opportunity itself in the founder workspace.
      await row.getByRole('link', { name: new RegExp(`^Open scope to review: ${BUSINESS}`) }).click()
      await expect(founder.page).toHaveURL(new RegExp(`/expansion\\?tab=pipeline&opportunity=${oppId}`))
      await expect(founder.page.getByRole('heading', { name: BUSINESS })).toBeVisible()

      const detail = await api(p1.context, `/api/partner/pipeline?id=${oppId}`)
      expect(detail.body.opportunity.status).toBe('more_information')
      expect(JSON.stringify(detail.body)).not.toMatch(/confirm booking provider|founder_assignment|takes technical scoping/)
      expect((detail.body.timeline as { label: string }[]).map((t) => t.label)).toContain('ScaleSmiths asked for more information')
      // [API] Partners cannot open the command centre.
      expect([401, 403]).toContain((await api(p1.context, '/api/expansion/command')).status)
      expect(await ledger(su)).toBe(ledgerBefore)
    })

"""

p='docs/expansion/ascend/B2-IMPLEMENTATION-STATUS.md'; s=open(p,encoding='utf8').read()
a='## B2.3 – B2.7: Not started\n'
assert s.count(a)==1
s=s.replace(a,'''## B2.3 Founder sales command centre: Implemented (browser evidence pending CI)

- **Branch:** `feature/operation-ascend-b2-3`, stacked on B2.2 and B2.1. Review after #166 and #167.
- **Where:** `/expansion/command` (founder page; `/expansion/*` already requires `expansion.manage`) and `GET/POST /api/expansion/command` (policy rule `ascend.command`). It is linked from the founder workspace overview when switched on.
- **Switch:** `FOUNDER_SALES_COMMAND_ENABLED` (default off).
- **Overview:** active opportunities, scopes awaiting review, scopes needing technical scoping, meetings to decide, partner help requests, approved without a contract, contracts accepted, stalled, applications to review, invited but not activated, and failed partner emails. All counts come from one repeatable-read snapshot.
- **Work queue:** seven kinds in a published order, oldest first within each kind (the rule is shown on the page). Every item opens a real destination: the opportunity itself (`/expansion?tab=pipeline&opportunity=<id>`, a new deep link in the founder workspace), the meetings tab or recruitment. Thresholds: stalled after 21 days without recorded activity (status change, audit entry or partner interaction); proposal follow-up 7 days after approval.
- **Partner oversight:** sorted alphabetically, never ranked. Shows status, region, open opportunities, contracts accepted and open help requests. Commission earned and paid come from `getExpansionFinance`, the Commission centre's own function. No learning data is read.
- **Assignment:** migration `0100_ascend_founder_assignments`, append-only. Each row supersedes exactly one earlier row: a unique `supersedes_id`, one root per opportunity, and a trigger that keeps the chain within one opportunity. It is a compare-and-set on the current assignment (a stale view gets 409; a concurrent duplicate is refused by the database). Every change needs a reason, is audited (`founder_assignment`), never touches `partner_id` or commission, sends no notification, and is never shown to the partner.
- **Ownership transfer between partners:** not implemented (FD-ASC-03).
- **Relationship to B1.7 (#163):** `founderOperations` is unchanged, to avoid conflicting with #163, which extends it. Once #163 merges, its queue additions (agreements needing attention, undelivered email) can be read here too.
- **Tests (local):**
  - `sales-command.test.ts` (order, ages, destinations, validation);
  - `sales-command.database.test.ts` (PGlite, 8 cases: off by default and founder-only; real counts and queue order with destinations; activity un-stalls; alphabetical oversight with Commission centre figures; assign, reassign and release with history and audit while ownership is unchanged; one of two simultaneous assignments admitted; database refuses a second root or a cross-opportunity chain; refusals);
  - RBAC 72/72.
- **Database:** 0100 applies on disposable PostgreSQL 16.14 and 14.25 (admin 101/101); history check passes.
- **Financial impact:** none (reads the existing finance summary; writes no financial record).

## B2.4 – B2.7: Not started
''')
open(p,'w',encoding='utf8').write(s)
p='docs/expansion/ascend/B2-ROADMAP.md'; s=open(p,encoding='utf8').read()
s=s.replace('| 3 | B2.3 Founder sales command centre | B2.1, #163 | Not started |','| 3 | B2.3 Founder sales command centre | B2.1, #163 | Implemented on `feature/operation-ascend-b2-3` (stacked), switched off; `founderOperations` left untouched for #163 |')
open(p,'w',encoding='utf8').write(s)
p='docs/expansion/ascend/B2-SECURITY-MODEL.md'; s=open(p,encoding='utf8').read()
a='## Threats considered\n'
s=s.replace(a,'''## B2.3 additions

| Boundary | Enforcement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| Founder only | `/expansion/command` page guard and `ascend.command` policy rule (`expansion.manage`), re-checked against the live session | database test "is off by default and founder-only"; browser Journey B |
| Concurrent assignment | Compare-and-set on the current assignment, plus unique `supersedes_id` and one root per opportunity | "admits exactly one of two simultaneous assignments" |
| No entitlement change | Assignment never writes `expansion_opportunities.partner_id`; no partner notification | database and browser tests assert ownership unchanged |
| No ranking or private data | Partners alphabetical; no Academy or learning tables read | "lists partners alphabetically…" |
| Bounded queries | Each queue source ≤ 200 rows, partners ≤ 1000, one repeatable-read snapshot | code review |

'''+a,1)
open(p,'w',encoding='utf8').write(s)
PYEOF
echo ok

## Summary

- alphabetical partner oversight, with commission figures from the Commission centre's own function.

Founders can record which of them is handling an opportunity. That record is internal and audited, and it never changes the partner's ownership or commission.

- [x] `feat`
- [ ] `fix`

- [x] CI/tooling
- [ ] Documentation only

```text
npx vitest run src/lib/sales-command.test.ts src/lib/server/sales-command.database.test.ts src/lib/rbac-authorization.test.ts  -> 65 passed

```

## Migrations

- [ ] No database migration.
- [x] Migration included and documented below.

`0100_ascend_founder_assignments` (after 0098 and 0099): forward-only and additive.
- **Table:** `expansion_founder_assignments` (append-only via `commercial_history_immutable`), with a unique `supersedes_id`, a partial unique index allowing one root per opportunity, and a lookup index.
- **Trigger:** an insert trigger keeps each chain within one opportunity. Trigger functions need no runtime grant.
- **Registration:** journal, shared plan and checksum manifest.

## Environment

- [ ] No environment-variable change.
- [x] Environment variables added to `.env.example` and documented below.

`FOUNDER_SALES_COMMAND_ENABLED` (admin app, default `false`): page and API return 404 and no link appears while it is off. CI turns it on for the disposable acceptance server only.

## Security and Privacy

- [x] No secrets, provider credentials, real `.env` files, database dumps, or
      client-private exports are included.
- [x] Admin/Forge access control and generated-workspace isolation are preserved.
- [x] Public analytics remains minimised and consent-aware.

- **Founder only:** the page guard (`/expansion/*`) and policy rule `ascend.command` (`expansion.manage`) are re-checked against the live session.
- **Assignments:**
  - compare-and-set (a stale view gets 409), and the database refuses a concurrent duplicate (tested with simultaneous calls);
  - a reason and an audit entry for each change;
  - no partner notification, and no write to `partner_id`.
- **Partner oversight:** never ranked; no learning data read.
- **Partner view:** the assignment and founder notes never appear in the partner's history (asserted in the browser journey).

## Evidence

Journey B in `ascend-pipeline.spec.ts` covers:
- the founder (signed in with MFA) opens the command centre;
- filters to scope reviews and sees the technical-scoping tag;
- axe and screenshots at six widths;
- assigns themselves with a reason;
- a stale assignment is refused with 409, and the partner's ownership is unchanged;
- "Open" deep-links to the opportunity itself;
- an authorised `review_scope` decision, with audit rows for both;
- the partner sees "ScaleSmiths asked for more information" without the internal note or assignment;
- partners are refused;
- the commission ledger is unchanged.

## Residual Risk and Follow-up

- FD-ASC-03: transferring an opportunity between partners is deliberately not implemented.
- When #163 merges, its additions to `founderOperations` (agreements needing attention, undelivered email retry) should be linked from this queue. `founderOperations` is untouched here to avoid a conflict.
- Thresholds (21 days stalled, 7 days proposal follow-up) are constants and could become founder settings.
- B2.4 to B2.7 are not started.

## Rollback

Revert the commit. The switch is off. Migration 0100 is additive and nothing else reads the table. There is no down-migration (forward-only policy).

content.thinking: The metric notes render bold and stack badly on phones, and the admin shell scrolls an inner container, so full-page shots miss the work queue. I'm fixing the CSS and adding a queue-focused capture next.

input.command:
cd /d/tmp/ss-ascend/admin && python - <<'PYEOF'
p='src/components/ascend/command.css'; s=open(p,encoding='utf8').read()
a='.sc-metrics{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fill,minmax(180px,1fr));'
assert s.count(a)==1
s=s.replace(a,'.sc-metrics{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fill,minmax(min(100%,150px),1fr));')
s=s.replace('.sc-metrics .sc-note{margin:0;','.sc-metrics .sc-note{margin:0;font-weight:400;')
s=s.replace('@media (max-width:760px){.sc{padding:20px 16px 40px}','@media (max-width:760px){.sc{padding:20px 16px 40px}.sc-metrics{grid-template-columns:repeat(2,minmax(0,1fr))}.sc-metrics dd{font-size:22px}')
open(p,'w',encoding='utf8').write(s)
p='test/e2e/ascend-pipeline.spec.ts'; s=open(p,encoding='utf8').read()
a="      await shots(founder.page, 'command-centre')\n"
assert s.count(a)==1
s=s.replace(a,a+"      await shots(founder.page, 'command-centre-queue', false, async () => { await row.scrollIntoViewIfNeeded() })\n      await shots(founder.page, 'command-centre-partners', false, async () => { await founder.page.locator('#sc-partners').scrollIntoViewIfNeeded() })\n")
open(p,'w',encoding='utf8').write(s)
PYEOF

content.text:
B2.3 is built and open as draft PR [#168](https://github.com/TheFridey/ScaleSmiths/pull/168), switched off by `FOUNDER_SALES_COMMAND_ENABLED`. CI is fully green on its final head, including the founder browser journey. It's stacked on [#166](https://github.com/TheFridey/ScaleSmiths/pull/166) and [#167](https://github.com/TheFridey/ScaleSmiths/pull/167), so review it after those.

**What founders get at `/expansion/command`**
- **Overview:** eleven counts, all read at the same moment from live records. They cover active opportunities, scopes waiting for review and those needing technical scoping, meetings to decide, partner help requests, approved scopes with no contract, contracts accepted, stalled opportunities, applications to review, partners invited but not activated, and failed partner emails.
- **Work queue:** seven kinds of item in a fixed order that's explained on the page, oldest first within each kind. There's no hidden score.
  - "Open" goes straight to the record. The founder workspace now accepts `?tab=…&opportunity=…` links, so a scope review opens that opportunity.
  - "Stalled" means 21 days with no recorded activity; proposal follow-up starts 7 days after approval.
- **Partner oversight:** alphabetical and never ranked. Commission earned and paid come from the same function the Commission centre uses, so the two can't disagree. No learning data is read.
- **Assigning a founder (migration 0100):** founders can record which of them is handling an opportunity.
  - Every change needs a reason and goes into the audit log.
  - If two founders act on the same view at once, only one succeeds and the other gets a "reload" message. This is tested with simultaneous requests.
  - It never changes the partner's ownership or commission, sends no notification, and never appears to the partner.
- **Not built:** moving an opportunity from one partner to another, which is your decision FD-ASC-03.
- **#163 (B1.7):** I left the existing founder queue code untouched, because #163 changes it. That way #163 merges cleanly.

**Checks**
- 65 unit and database tests pass. Lint and typecheck are clean. Migration 0100 applies on PostgreSQL 14 and 16.
- **Founder journey in the browser:** the founder signs in with MFA, opens the centre and filters to scope reviews.
  - Assigning a founder works, and a second assignment from an out-of-date view is refused.
  - "Open" lands on the opportunity, and the founder records an "ask for more information" decision.
  - The partner sees that outcome but not the internal note or the assignment.
  - Partners are refused, and the commission ledger is unchanged.
- **Fixed along the way:** the accessibility scan caught invalid list markup in the metric cards. The screenshots showed bold note text and cards stacking one per row on phones, and a test pattern was missing an escape character.
- I looked at the screenshots of the overview, queue and partner table at all six widths. They're committed in `docs/expansion/ascend/evidence/b2-1/`.

**One flaky finance test.** An existing race test ("withdrawal request versus unpaid-refund adjustment") failed once on an earlier head, then passed.
- **Withdrawal first:** the refund is refused, which is the only ordering the test expects.
- **Refund first:** the withdrawal then reserves the net amount, including the negative adjustment. Both legitimately succeed, and commission is still never both reserved and reduced.

So the test's assumption is wrong, not the ledger. It's in the finance suite, so I've left it alone and recorded the diagnosis on #168.

import "server-only"

import { and, eq } from "drizzle-orm"
import { db } from "@/lib/db"
import { monthlyReports } from "@/lib/schema"

export async function getReportingDashboardSnapshot(month: number, year: number) {
  const reports = await db.select({ clientId: monthlyReports.clientId })
    .from(monthlyReports)
    .where(and(eq(monthlyReports.month, month), eq(monthlyReports.year, year)))
  return { currentMonthReportCount: reports.length, clientIdsWithCurrentReport: new Set(reports.map((report) => report.clientId)) }
}
CREATE TABLE "invoices" (
	"id" serial PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL,
	"invoice_number" text,
	"client_id" integer NOT NULL,
	"sequence_number" integer,
	"client_code_snapshot" text,
	"client_name_snapshot" text NOT NULL,
	"billing_contact_name_snapshot" text,
	"billing_email_snapshot" text,
	"billing_address_line_1_snapshot" text,
	"billing_address_line_2_snapshot" text,
	"billing_city_snapshot" text,
	"billing_county_snapshot" text,
	"billing_postcode_snapshot" text,
	"billing_country_snapshot" text,
	"currency" text DEFAULT 'GBP' NOT NULL,
	"invoice_date" timestamp with time zone NOT NULL,
	"due_date" timestamp with time zone NOT NULL,
	"status" "invoice_status" DEFAULT 'draft' NOT NULL,
	"subtotal" integer NOT NULL,
	"total" integer NOT NULL,
	"internal_notes" text,
	"customer_notes" text,
	"issued_at" timestamp with time zone,
	"paid_at" timestamp with time zone,
	"voided_at" timestamp with time zone,
	"document_template_version" text,
	"supplier_snapshot" jsonb,
	"payment_snapshot" jsonb,
CREATE TABLE commercial_contracts (
 id serial PRIMARY KEY, client_id integer NOT NULL REFERENCES clients(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
 prospect_id integer REFERENCES prospects(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
 category text NOT NULL CHECK (category IN ('retainer','premium_partnership','website_build','growth_audit','performance')),
 status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft' CHECK (status IN ('draft','confirmed','ended')),
 monthly_amount integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (monthly_amount >= 0), one_off_amount integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (one_off_amount >= 0),
 evidence text NOT NULL, starts_at timestamptz NOT NULL, ends_at timestamptz,
 actor_user_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES admin_users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
 version integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 1, created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
 CHECK (ends_at IS NULL OR ends_at > starts_at), CHECK (category IN ('retainer','premium_partnership') OR monthly_amount=0)
);
CREATE TABLE commercial_payments (
 id serial PRIMARY KEY, client_id integer NOT NULL REFERENCES clients(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
 invoice_id integer REFERENCES invoices(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
 category text NOT NULL CHECK (category IN ('retainer','premium_partnership','website_build','growth_audit','performance')),
 amount integer NOT NULL CHECK (amount <> 0), evidence text NOT NULL,
 reference text NOT NULL UNIQUE, reverses_payment_id integer UNIQUE REFERENCES commercial_payments(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
 actor_user_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES admin_users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
 received_at timestamptz NOT NULL, created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
 CHECK ((amount>0 AND reverses_payment_id IS NULL) OR (amount<0 AND reverses_payment_id IS NOT NULL))
);
CREATE TABLE commercial_forecasts (
 id serial PRIMARY KEY, client_id integer NOT NULL REFERENCES clients(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
 amount integer NOT NULL CHECK (amount>=0), expected_at timestamptz NOT NULL, notes text NOT NULL,
 actor_user_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES admin_users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
 created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE TABLE commercial_settings (
 key text PRIMARY KEY, value jsonb NOT NULL, version integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 1, updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

export async function commercialSnapshot(actor: Actor) {
  const finance = hasCapability(actor.role, "finance.read")
  const [
    leads,
    activities,
    contacts,
    tasks,
    users,
    settings,
    history,
    clientRows,
    contracts,
    payments,
    forecasts,
    invoiceRows,
    proposals,
  ] = await Promise.all([
    db
      .select()
      .from(prospects)
      .where(isNull(prospects.archivedAt))
      .orderBy(desc(prospects.updatedAt)),
    db
      .select()
      .from(outreachActivities)
      .orderBy(desc(outreachActivities.createdAt)),
    db.select().from(commercialContacts),
    db.select().from(commercialTasks).orderBy(commercialTasks.dueAt),
    db
      .select({
        id: adminUsers.id,
        displayName: adminUsers.displayName,
        role: adminUsers.role,
        founderTargets: sql<Record<
          string,
          number
        > | null>`case when lower(${adminUsers.email}) in ('admin@scalesmiths.co.uk', 'trev@scalesmiths.co.uk') then '{"connections":1,"connectionStretch":2}'::jsonb else null end`
      })
      .from(adminUsers)
      .where(eq(adminUsers.active, true)),
    db.select().from(commercialSettings),
    db
      .select()
      .from(commercialAudit)
      .orderBy(desc(commercialAudit.createdAt))
      .limit(500),
    hasCapability(actor.role, "clients.read")
      ? db.select({ id: clients.id, name: clients.name }).from(clients)
      : [],
    finance ? db.select().from(commercialContracts) : [],
    finance ? db.select().from(commercialPayments) : [],
    finance ? db.select().from(commercialForecasts) : [],
    finance
      ? db
          .select({
            id: invoices.id,
            clientId: invoices.clientId,
            invoiceNumber: invoices.invoiceNumber,
            status: invoices.status,
            total: invoices.total,

export async function commercialSnapshot(actor: Actor) {
  const finance = hasCapability(actor.role, "finance.read")
  const [
    leads,
    activities,
    contacts,
    tasks,
    users,
    settings,
    history,
    clientRows,
    contracts,
    payments,
    forecasts,
    invoiceRows,
    proposals,
  ] = await Promise.all([
    db
      .select()
      .from(prospects)
      .where(isNull(prospects.archivedAt))
      .orderBy(desc(prospects.updatedAt)),
    db
      .select()
      .from(outreachActivities)
      .orderBy(desc(outreachActivities.createdAt)),
    db.select().from(commercialContacts),
    db.select().from(commercialTasks).orderBy(commercialTasks.dueAt),
    db
      .select({
        id: adminUsers.id,
        displayName: adminUsers.displayName,
        role: adminUsers.role,
        founderTargets: sql<Record<
          string,
          number
        > | null>`case when lower(${adminUsers.email}) in ('admin@scalesmiths.co.uk', 'trev@scalesmiths.co.uk') then '{"connections":1,"connectionStretch":2}'::jsonb else null end`

      .from(adminUsers)

      .from(commercialAudit)

    finance ? db.select().from(commercialContracts) : [],

    finance ? db.select().from(commercialForecasts) : [],
    finance

    },
    leads,

    settings,
    history: history.filter(
      (h) => finance || !["contract", "payment", "forecast"].includes(h.entity),
    ),
    clients: clientRows,
    contracts,
    payments,
    forecasts,
    invoices: invoiceRows,
    proposals,
    defaults: {
      config: DEFAULT_COMMERCIAL_CONFIG,
      targets: DEFAULT_COMPANY_TARGETS,
    },
    serverTime: new Date().toISOString(),
  }
}

-- Operation Ascend B2.4: founder-entered forecast assumptions, versioned. Forward-only and additive.
-- Forecasts are hypothetical. This table is the only thing B2.4 writes; no financial table (payments, invoices, contracts,
-- commission ledger, payouts) is ever written by forecasting, and nothing in the finance engine reads this table.
CREATE TABLE expansion_forecast_assumptions (
 id uuid PRIMARY KEY,
 scenario text NOT NULL CHECK (scenario IN ('conservative','baseline','optimistic')),
 version integer NOT NULL CHECK (version > 0),
 qualified_bp integer NOT NULL CHECK (qualified_bp BETWEEN 0 AND 10000),
 scope_submitted_bp integer NOT NULL CHECK (scope_submitted_bp BETWEEN 0 AND 10000),
 approved_bp integer NOT NULL CHECK (approved_bp BETWEEN 0 AND 10000),
 average_value_pence bigint NOT NULL CHECK (average_value_pence BETWEEN 0 AND 999999999999),
 monthly_retention_bp integer NOT NULL CHECK (monthly_retention_bp BETWEEN 0 AND 10000),
 horizon_months integer NOT NULL CHECK (horizon_months BETWEEN 1 AND 24),
 rationale text NOT NULL CHECK (length(btrim(rationale)) BETWEEN 3 AND 1000),
 created_by uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES admin_users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
 created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
 UNIQUE (scenario, version)
);
CREATE TRIGGER expansion_forecast_assumptions_immutable BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE ON expansion_forecast_assumptions FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION commercial_history_immutable();

-- Operation Ascend B2.4: founder-entered forecast assumptions, versioned. Forward-only and additive.
-- Forecasts are hypothetical. This table is the only thing B2.4 writes; no financial table (payments, invoices, contracts,
-- commission ledger, payouts) is ever written by forecasting, and nothing in the finance engine reads this table.
CREATE TABLE expansion_forecast_assumptions (
 id uuid PRIMARY KEY,
 scenario text NOT NULL CHECK (scenario IN ('conservative','baseline','optimistic')),
 version integer NOT NULL CHECK (version > 0),
 qualified_bp integer NOT NULL CHECK (qualified_bp BETWEEN 0 AND 10000),
 scope_submitted_bp integer NOT NULL CHECK (scope_submitted_bp BETWEEN 0 AND 10000),
 approved_bp integer NOT NULL CHECK (approved_bp BETWEEN 0 AND 10000),
 average_value_pence bigint NOT NULL CHECK (average_value_pence BETWEEN 0 AND 999999999999),
 monthly_retention_bp integer NOT NULL CHECK (monthly_retention_bp BETWEEN 0 AND 10000),
 horizon_months integer NOT NULL CHECK (horizon_months BETWEEN 1 AND 24),
 rationale text NOT NULL CHECK (length(btrim(rationale)) BETWEEN 3 AND 1000),
 created_by uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES admin_users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
 created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
 UNIQUE (scenario, version)
);
CREATE TRIGGER expansion_forecast_assumptions_immutable BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE ON expansion_forecast_assumptions FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION commercial_history_immutable();

      const paid = (await su.query("insert into commercial_payments(client_id,category,amount,evidence,reference,actor_user_id,received_at) values($1,'website_build',150000,'TEST ONLY',$2,$3,now()) returning id", [client, `TEST-REV-${run}-1`, founderId])).rows[0].id
      await su.query("insert into commercial_payments(client_id,category,amount,evidence,reference,actor_user_id,received_at,reverses_payment_id) values($1,'website_build',-150000,'TEST ONLY reversal',$2,$3,now(),$4)", [client, `TEST-REV-${run}-2`, founderId, paid])
      await su.query("insert into commercial_payments(client_id,category,amount,evidence,reference,actor_user_id,received_at) values($1,'retainer',25000,'TEST ONLY',$2,$3,now())", [client, `TEST-REV-${run}-3`, founderId])
      const sums = (await su.query("select coalesce(sum(amount),0)::text collected,coalesce(sum(amount) filter (where amount<0),0)::text reversals from commercial_payments")).rows[0]
      const ledgerSums = (await su.query("select (select coalesce(sum(amount_pence),0) from expansion_commission_ledger)::text earned,(select coalesce(sum(amount_pence),0) from expansion_payouts where status='paid')::text paid")).rows[0]

          select 'payments' t, md5(coalesce(string_agg(x::text,'|' order by x.id),'')) h from commercial_payments x union all
          select 'invoices', md5(coalesce(string_agg(x::text,'|' order by x.id),'')) from invoices x union all
          select 'contracts', md5(coalesce(string_agg(x::text,'|' order by x.id),'')) from commercial_contracts x union all
          select 'ledger', md5(coalesce(string_agg(x::text,'|' order by x.id::text),'')) from expansion_commission_ledger x union all
          select 'payouts', md5(coalesce(string_agg(x::text,'|' order by x.id::text),'')) from expansion_payouts x) f`)).rows[0].h as string
      const financeBefore = await fingerprintFinance()

      expect(rev.body.actual.reversalsPence).toBe(sums.reversals)
      expect(rev.body.actual.commission.earnedPence).toBe(ledgerSums.earned)
      expect(rev.body.actual.commission.paidPence).toBe(ledgerSums.paid)
      // [UI] Actual and projected sections are separate and labelled.
      await founder.page.goto(`${origin()}/expansion/revenue`)
      await expect(founder.page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Revenue intelligence' })).toBeVisible()
      await expect(founder.page.getByText('Actual · verified records')).toBeVisible()
      await expect(founder.page.getByText('Projection · hypothetical, not money earned')).toBeVisible()
      await expect(founder.page.locator('.rv-actual').getByText('Verified collected revenue')).toBeVisible()
      await axe(founder.page, '.sc', 'revenue intelligence')
      await shots(founder.page, 'revenue-actual')
      // [UI] C6-C7 Assumptions are disclosed; a what-if updates on the page; saving records a version.
      const baseline = founder.page.getByRole('tabpanel', { name: 'Baseline' })
      const form = baseline.getByRole('form', { name: 'Baseline assumptions' })
      await form.getByLabel('Qualified: chance of acceptance (%)').fill('10')
      await form.getByLabel('Scope under review: chance of acceptance (%)').fill('30')
      await form.getByLabel('Scope approved: chance of acceptance (%)').fill('70')
      await form.getByLabel('Assumed average contract value (£)').fill('3000')
      await form.getByLabel('Recurring revenue kept each month (%)').fill('95')
      await form.getByLabel(/^Horizon/).fill('3')
      await expect(baseline.getByLabel('Baseline projection')).toBeVisible()
      await form.getByLabel('Why these assumptions (recorded with the version)').fill('TEST ONLY founder estimate for the journey')
      await form.getByRole('button', { name: 'Save as new version' }).click()
      await expect(founder.page.getByRole('tabpanel', { name: 'Baseline' }).getByText(/^Saved version \d+ by TEST ONLY Founder A/)).toBeVisible()
      await founder.page.getByRole('tab', { name: 'Baseline' }).focus()
      await founder.page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight')
      await expect(founder.page.getByRole('tab', { name: 'Optimistic' })).toHaveAttribute('aria-selected', 'true')
      await expect(founder.page.getByRole('tab', { name: 'Optimistic' })).toBeFocused()
      await founder.page.getByRole('tab', { name: 'Baseline' }).click()
      await baseline.getByLabel('Baseline projection').scrollIntoViewIfNeeded()
      await axe(founder.page, '.sc', 'revenue forecast')
      await shots(founder.page, 'revenue-forecast', false, async () => { await founder.page.getByRole('tabpanel', { name: 'Baseline' }).getByLabel('Baseline projection').scrollIntoViewIfNeeded() })
      // C8 No financial record changed; partners cannot read revenue.
      expect(await fingerprintFinance()).toBe(financeBefore)
      expect([401, 403]).toContain((await api(p1.context, '/api/expansion/revenue')).status)
    })

"""
s=s.replace(a,step+a)
open(p,'w',encoding='utf8').write(s)

f=/d/Hermes/temp/claude/4ef63fda3fc46ec8/66dcb166-1645-4bd3-8607-1865b90aeffc/scratchpad/b24-pr.md && cat > $f <<'EOF'
## Summary

Operation Ascend B2.4, switched off by `REVENUE_INTELLIGENCE_ENABLED`. **Stacked on #166, #167 and #168: review after them; this PR's own change is the last code commit.** `/expansion/revenue` shows founders with finance access actual revenue from the existing authoritative records and their existing definitions. Hypothetical forecasts sit in a clearly separated section. Forecasting writes nothing financial: only versioned assumptions in their own table.

## Type

- [x] `feat`
- [ ] `fix`
- [x] `test`
- [x] `docs`
- [ ] `refactor`
- [ ] `security`
- [ ] `perf`
- [ ] `chore`

## Scope

- [ ] Public web
- [x] Admin
- [ ] Forge
- [x] Database/migrations
- [ ] Docker/deployment/Nginx
- [x] CI/tooling
- [ ] Documentation only

## Validation

Commands run, with results:

```text
npx vitest run src/lib/revenue-forecast.test.ts src/lib/server/revenue-intelligence.database.test.ts src/lib/rbac-authorization.test.ts  -> 63 passed
npx eslint <changed files>                                                                                                              -> clean
npx tsc --noEmit                                                                                                                        -> no project errors
npm run test:db:migrate on disposable PostgreSQL 16.14 and 14.25                                                                        -> "admin 102/102" on both
node scripts/check-migration-history.mjs                                                                                                -> "52 historical and 75 forward migrations are locked"
```

Commands not run, and why:

```text
Journey C browser step (added to ascend-pipeline.spec.ts): runs in CI's Empower Browser Acceptance; results to follow as a comment.
Full admin unit suite locally: machine too slow; CI's Admin job is authoritative.
```

## Migrations

- [ ] No database migration.
- [x] Migration included and documented below.

`0101_ascend_forecast_assumptions`: forward-only and additive.
- **Table:** `expansion_forecast_assumptions`, one row per scenario version, unique on (scenario, version). It is append-only via `commercial_history_immutable`.
- **Checks:** CHECK constraints bound the basis points, value and horizon.
- **Isolation:** nothing in the finance engine reads it.
- **Registration:** journal, shared plan and checksums.

## Environment

- [ ] No environment-variable change.
- [x] Environment variables added to `.env.example` and documented below.

`REVENUE_INTELLIGENCE_ENABLED` (admin app, default `false`). CI turns it on only for the disposable acceptance server.

## Security and Privacy

- [x] No secrets, provider credentials, real `.env` files, database dumps, or
      client-private exports are included.
- [x] Admin/Forge access control and generated-workspace isolation are preserved.
- [x] Public analytics remains minimised and consent-aware.

- **Access:** policy rule `ascend.revenue` (`expansion.manage`) plus a live `finance.read` check. Partners, finance-only staff and revoked sessions are refused (tested).
- **Input validation:** assumptions are validated as integer basis points, whole pence and a bounded horizon, on the server and by the database.

## Evidence

**Service-level Journey C** (`revenue-intelligence.database.test.ts`, seeded with hand-calculated figures):
- collected £1,000.00 net of a £200.00 reversal;
- partner-attributed £550.00;
- outstanding £1,100.00 across 2 issued invoices (draft, void and paid excluded);
- contracted monthly recurring £750.00;
- commission earned, paid and liability passed through from the Commission centre;
- the twelve-month window;
- no historical rate with 3 closed outcomes;
- three saved versions with a fingerprint of no financial table changed;
- an exact projection of £5,032.39 (calculation shown in the test).

**Browser Journey C** (`ascend-pipeline.spec.ts`):
- TEST ONLY payments and a reversal are seeded on the disposable database;
- the API figures equal SQL sums over payments, ledger and payouts;
- the actual and projection sections are separate and labelled;
- axe passes;
- a what-if projection appears and saving records a version;
- the scenario tabs work with arrow keys;
- payments, invoices, contracts, ledger and payouts are unchanged (fingerprint);
- partners are refused.

## Residual Risk and Follow-up

- **FD-ASC-05:** whether 10 closed outcomes is the right minimum before a historical rate is shown.
- **Pipeline value:** the forecast uses one assumed average value per scenario. A per-opportunity value does not exist until a contract is accepted.
- **Partner commission views:** unchanged. The existing partner Commission centre already covers earned, pending, adjustments, withdrawals and history.
- **Remaining slices:** B2.5 to B2.7 not started.

## Rollback

Revert the commit. The switch is off, and 0101 is additive and read by nothing else. There is no down-migration (forward-only policy).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF

content.text:
B2.4 is built and open as draft PR [#169](https://github.com/TheFridey/ScaleSmiths/pull/169), switched off by `REVENUE_INTELLIGENCE_ENABLED`. Full CI was green on the last code change, including the revenue browser journey; the commit after it adds only screenshots and docs. It's stacked on #166 to #168, so review it after those.

**Revenue to date** (`/expansion/revenue`, founders with finance access only)
- **Collected revenue:** all recorded payments, with reversals shown separately. It's also split by service and by month (last 12 months, London time), and splits out recurring, one-off builds and partner-attributed collections.
- **Outstanding invoiced:** issued invoices minus payments recorded against them, labelled "not revenue until collected".
- **Contracted monthly recurring:** calculated by the Command Centre's existing function.
- **Commission earned, paid and liability:** read from the Commission centre's own function, so the two pages can't disagree.

Nothing here is a new source of truth; every figure uses the definitions these records already have.

**Forecast**
- It sits in a separately styled section labelled "Projection · hypothetical, not money earned".
- **Pipeline:** each stage's opportunity count × your probability for that stage × your assumed contract value.
- **Recurring:** today's contracted monthly revenue, reduced each month by your retention assumption, over 1–24 months.
- **Arithmetic:** done in whole pence with no rounding drift, and every component's calculation is shown.
- **No invented rates:** there are no default probabilities or values. A historical conversion rate appears only once 10 opportunities have closed (FD-ASC-05); until then the page says how many have.
- **Command Centre estimates:** the expected payments founders entered there are listed separately and labelled as estimates.
- **Scenarios:** Conservative, Baseline and Optimistic. Changing a figure updates the projection on the page only. "Save as new version" records the assumptions and your reason in their own append-only table (migration 0101). No financial table is written.
- **Partner commission:** partners' existing commission page already shows earned, pending, adjustments, withdrawals and history, so I didn't duplicate it. The 30% rate and the £705 illustration are unchanged.

**Checks**
- **Database tests:** five tests against hand-calculated figures. Examples:
  - £1,000.00 collected after a £200.00 reversal;
  - £1,100.00 outstanding across two issued invoices;
  - a projection of exactly £5,032.39.
  Saving three assumption versions left every financial table byte-identical. Partners, finance-only staff and revoked sessions are refused.
- **Browser journey:** test payments and a reversal are seeded on the throwaway CI database. The page's figures match SQL totals over payments, the commission ledger and payouts.
  - Saving a scenario works, and the scenario tabs work with arrow keys.
  - Payments, invoices, contracts, the ledger and payouts are unchanged afterwards.
  - The accessibility scan passes.
- **Migration:** 0101 applies on PostgreSQL 14 and 16.
- **Fixed after looking at the screenshots:** the projection table was cramped on phones (now stacked cards), and the wording read "Only 0 closed outcomes".

**The flaky finance test has now failed twice**, once on #168 and once on this PR's first run. Both times it was the same race test, and these PRs don't touch finance code. The test only expects one of two valid orderings, so it's a flaw in the test, not the ledger. It will keep turning PRs red at random until it's fixed. It's a small test-only change in the finance suite, but I'd want your go-ahead before touching that suite.

content.thinking: Both new tests passed all 10 runs and the full withdrawal suite is green (12/12), which shows the old assertion was wrong since both operations legitimately succeed in refund-first order. I'm linting and then opening the PR.

input.command:
npx eslint test/integration/expansion-concurrency.integration.test.ts 2>&1 | tail -4; echo lint=$?; cd .. && git status --short | grep -v node_modules.partial; git add admin/test/integration/expansion-concurrency.integration.test.ts && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
test(expansion): accept both valid orders in the withdrawal versus unpaid-refund race

The test assumed that whichever of a withdrawal request and an unpaid-
refund adjustment won, the other was refused. Both take the same partner
row lock, but an adjust_unpaid refund opens no refund review, so when the
adjustment commits first the request legitimately succeeds and reserves
the new negative entry with the original one. The test then failed
intermittently in CI (twice on #168/#169) with two fulfilled results.

The race now accepts either order and asserts the invariant directly:
the request always succeeds, the reservation equals the partner's net
ledger total, and no negative adjustment is left unreserved. A new
deterministic test commits the adjustment first and checks the request
reserves only the net £240. Test-only; no product or ledger code changes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git push -q -u origin fix/withdrawal-refund-race-test 2>&1 | tail -1; git log --oneline -1
